text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing steady RSS growth on kv-cache in prod-gpu-6 for long-chat workloads (~30k tokens). Not a single leak but fragmentation creeping up, evictions tick up, tail latency spikes around 99th.
maria: Short snapshot from the debug counters:
```
kv.stats():
  total_kv_bytes: 14.8GB
  used_bytes: 9.2GB
  free_fragment_pct: 38
  slab_buckets: {256: 124k, 512: 48k, 1024: 9k, 2048+: 1.2k}
  avg_alloc_size: 437
  compaction_runs_last_24h: 2
```
maria: Free OS memory is fine; kernel/page thrashing not showing, this looks allocator-level. Reproducer: run longcontext-runner w/ seed=42, seq-len-dist skewed to 800-1200 then occasional 6k tails. I can drop logs.
liam: Hmm. Sounds like bucket fragmentation — many ~500/1k allocations leaving small slivers in slabs. We're hitting the allocator's geometric growth step in an awkward region.
liam: Two immediate ideas:
  1) Adjust bucket-sizing: change growth factor from 2x to 1.5x around 256-2048 so fewer mid-sized buckets.
  2) Introduce lightweight in-slab coalescing: when two adjacent free blocks appear, merge them lazily during low-load ticks.
liam: Also propose a background compactor that only runs on nodes with frag_pct > 30% AND p95 latency headroom > 20ms. Should avoid adding latency under pressure.
anika: +1 on sampling metrics. We need per-model/reuse-window histograms to prove it's fragmentation, not just allocation churn.
anika: Suggest adding `kv.reuse_window_ms` and `kv.alloc_size_histogram` to the runtime metrics. If reuse_window for small blocks << compaction interval, compaction won't help.
rachel: For a canary plan: can we A/B the bucket tweak first? Changing growth factor seems reversible and low-risk.
liam: Yes. We can A/B on canary pool `dedicated-canary-3`. Steps:
  - build allocator flag `--bucket-growth=1.5` and `--compactor=false`
  - run for 24-48h, measure frag_pct, evictions, p99
  - if frag drops >10% and p99 not worse -> roll to more nodes
liam: Fallback: set flag back to 2.0 and drain.
maria: I'll prepare the perf job and attach the exact CLI. Also will push the sampled `alloc_size_hist` so you can see skew.
ops-bot: incident:kv-frag-high triggered on prod-gpu-6 at 1712348600 (auto-threshold frag_pct > 35%). Alert routed to eng-runtime oncall.
deploy-bot: Link to canary PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/4321 — includes allocator flag and a small compactor prototype.
rachel: If we add coalescing, we should gate it behind a runtime flag and ensure it's incremental (max 1 merge per request path) so we don't regress latency.
liam: Agreed. Implementation sketch:
```
// on free:
if (adjacent_free && compaction_budget > 0) {
  merge(); compaction_budget--;
}
// background: if frag_pct high and budget accumulated, run scan of hotspot slabs
```
liam: Also think about block-size TTL for tiny slices created by beam-search; expire unused tiny blocks faster to reduce stickiness.
anika: Important: correlate this with batching heuristics — large batches create different allocation patterns. Add `batch_size` tag to metrics.
maria: Thanks. I'll post the perf job + logs to #perf-runs and link here. Plan: start A/B tomorrow in morning window, monitor for 72h.
rachel: Sounds good. Assign owners? maria -> run perf/canary. liam -> implement flag + rollout automation. anika -> add metrics + dashboard. I'll coordinate dashboard alerts.
maria: assigning now, will ping when job is up. :eyes:
liam: I'll sketch compactor sprint ticket after we have canary results. :thumbsup:
